quasi-tile.look: Unmistakable Penrose rhomb floor at N=5: thick and thin rhombs, 5-fold stars and decagons, every tile the same two shapes, no long lines. Threshold on tile ids gives rhomb-edged blobs; TileType shows the two populations cleanly. N=4 reads as octagonal square and rhomb tiling, N=7 as dense 7-fold rosettes with three rhomb types. Bevel relief is the best relief in the family: convincing paving stones at varied heights. 3D is real rhombohedra: chunky faceted solids with crisp cut faces. Weak outputs: Lookup with Perlin in the tile frame is muddy and hides the tiles, and VertexDistance reads as soft dots with little order visible in the field, though its FFT has clear 10-fold spots.
quasi-tile.dims: Measured: 2D exact at N=4,5,7 rendered, N=9 bound-tested only. 3D exact: 20 triples x 8 candidates, 59999 of 60000 samples one hit, 1 double hit, volume ratio 2.6258 (phi^2 2.618). 4D not implemented, with a clear reason: an 8-grid would need about 70 x 16 = 1120 candidates (estimate), so z and w must pass through and GenTileable2D will not tile.
quasi-tile.node_shape: QuasiTile: Families {4,5,7}; Output enum {EdgeDistance, TileValue, TileType, Grouted, Bevel}; Grout Width hybrid; Bevel; Rotation; Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max. Drop Lookup and VertexDistance unless a Lookup at the tile centre proves better (not tested). Optional N=5 curve mask, see discoveries.
quasi-tile.port_notes: Bound result: 4 candidates per pair suffice, 40 for N=5, not the idea's 90. Requires the zonogon centre c = sum e_k / 2 in the estimate for even N; in 3D forgetting it gave |a-t| 1.05 and breaks the bound, with it 0.6973 against 0.809. Direct scalar no-early-out: N=4 128.2, N=5 222.0, N=7 565.4 ns; harness perlin2 50.2, worley2 109.5. Use margin selection rather than a hit test: a port gets 3 mins and 1 compare per candidate and always returns one tile (scalar branchy prototype 365 vs 261 ns, so the SIMD cost is an open question). Guard singular gamma: all-zero gave 0.38% bad samples. Zero-sum gamma gives true Penrose: vertex index census only 1 and 2, 149896 and 150104 of 300000. Float32 limit: bad samples .0003% at 100 tile edges from origin, .06% at 1e3, .16% at 1e4, .45% at 3e4, 1.8% at 1e5, 13.9% at 1e6. Margin selection does not fix the underlying error but hides it: 3e4 looks clean, 1e5 shows a few specks in the hillshade.

critic.notes: The only true aperiodic tiling in the family and it is exact. Ship for 2D and 3D; 4D does not exist and GenTileable2D would not tile, state that in the node description. N=7 (84 candidates) is twice N=5 cost, keep it but call it expensive. Float32 defects start to matter past about 1e4 tile edges from the origin; margin selection hides them, a port should offset the origin to the sample block or document the range. AVX2 cost estimate: scaling worley2 scalar to CellularDistance AVX2 (28:1) gives ~15 ns, the prototyper's 10:1 gives ~43 ns; call it 15-45 ns 2D N=5, estimate only.
critic.improved: Earlier critic pass added out=11 type pavers (prev) and out=10 tile-centre Lookup. I rendered out=10 as relief: stepped Penrose terraces following a smooth field, the most terrain-like image in the family.

tournament.notes: Exact Penrose (N=5), Ammann-Beenker (N=4) and 7-fold rhomb tilings located pointwise. Bound verified independently: 4 candidates per pair suffice, 1 rhomb per point at N=4..9, 0 outside floor/ceil over 1M points per N. Seeds 7 and 11 look the same. check c0ratio 7.90, range -1..1, far 4e4 ok, 3D rhombohedra real. Harness 433 ns = 8.2x perlin2 with margin select (prototyper quoted 5.5x for the branchy test). AVX2 15-45 ns 2D N=5 estimate, 3D est 100-200 ns, no 4D so GenTileable2D will not tile: document it. Float32 defects past ~1e4 tile edges; margin select hides them. Best relief in the family (type pavers, and the new tile-centre Lookup terraces).
tournament.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE, not measured, scaled about 10:1 from scalar no-early-out timings (from worley2 5x5 109.5 ns scalar vs CellularDistance 3x3 3.9 ns AVX2). 2D N=5 15-25, N=4 10-15, N=7 45-70. 3D 100-200. 4D not available.

artist-terrain.note: Unmistakable Penrose floor; bevel relief is convincing paving; vol is real rhombohedra; Penrose terraces discovery is terrain-usable. 15-45 ns 2D estimate, niche.

artist-material.note: Exact Penrose reads instantly, and the cube-stack relief and worm mask are great. Ornamental rather than everyday.

voxel-engineer.note: Immediately Penrose, and the terrace relief is striking. 100-200 ns est in 3D, no 4D. A 2D floor and plate node for me.

maintainer.note: Unmistakable Penrose floor, relief of tumbled rhomb blocks is one of the best images, candidate bound verified independently. 15-25 ns est 2D, 100-200 3D, no 4D so GenTileable2D will not tile. Ship 2D/3D with that caveat written on it.

graphics-researcher.note: Exact Penrose, Ammann-Beenker and 7-fold rhomb tilings located pointwise with an independently verified candidate bound; the bevel relief is convincing paving and nobody ships this. Lookup-centre terraces and Penrose curve masks extend it.

creative.note: Penrose in 2D, and the relief is a startling city of tilted cubes. Aperiodic with no visible lattice.

plan_node.expected_cost: Measured with fnlab bench, AVX2, 2D / 3D / 4D: 13.93 / 53.13 / 53.14 ns at Families Five, against Perlin 0.95 / 2.16 / 4.13 and CellularDistance 3.98 / 12.43 / 41.57 in the same run. SSE41 35.08 / 144.12 / 143.68, AVX512 11.65 / 43.72 / 43.76. 2D at Families Four 6.96, Seven 37.22. Same at any Output except CentreLookup, with a Perlin Lookup 16.59 / 81.33 / 78.53. 4D is the 3D form.
plan_node.dims: 2D at Families 4, 5, 7 and 3D real, each matched tile for tile against a double precision forward construction. NO 4D (about 1120 candidates by estimate): 4D ignores w. GenTileable2D wraps with no seam (fnlab tile ratio 0.47) but shows a warped slice through the rhombohedra with no rhombs, and rows v and -v are equal on 100.0% of pixels, so it mirrors top to bottom. The description says so.
plan_node.range: Native ranges by construction, no fitted constant. Value outputs are +-1, EdgeDistance is 0 to half the widest tile thickness (0.5 at Four, 0.4755 at Five, 0.4875 at Seven, 0.4253 in 3D), Bevel reaches 1 at the highest stone. Measured over 1M samples per dimension on 2 seeds: all of them -1.0000 to 1.0000 except EdgeDistance tops of 0.9945 to 0.9961 in 2D and 0.9714 in 3D, which random samples only approach at tile centres. CentreLookup passes Lookup through.
notes: Candidate bound re-proved by an independent double-precision forward construction: exactly one rhomb per point, 0 hits outside {floor t, ceil t}.

The prototype's float32 ceil gave bad samples of .06% at 1e3 tile edges, 1.8% at 1e5, 13.9% at 1e6. The port writes each tile relative to its crossing, which cancels the large terms, and gets ceil( t ) - t from wrapping 32 bit fixed point. A test compares tile identity to a double precision reference: tile wrong by more than 8 float steps on 0 of 120000 samples up to 3e4 tile edges, .0033% at 1e5, .1% at 1e6, 30% at 3e6, where float32 t breaks the candidate bound. Past 1e6 the description warns.

Thick / thin area ratio 2.6273 against phi^2 2.6180, lowest corner index only 1 or 2 at Families Five, so true Penrose. Singular gamma: 40 seeds including 0, +-1, INT_MAX and INT_MIN gave no sample off by more than 8 float steps.

Sharing line products between combinations was tried: 2% at Five, nothing at Seven, reverted. A runtime branch around the coordinate selects made AVX512 3D CentreLookup 66-143 ns and unstable, a template bool made it 50-54.

master.one_liner: Penrose rhombs (5-fold), Ammann-Beenker (8-fold) and other quasicrystal tilings evaluated pointwise through de Bruijn's multigrid dual with a bounded candidate search, so aperiodic floor tiles, girih-like ornament and quasicrystal etch patterns become a FastNoise node with edge distance, tile type and per-tile Source lookup.
master.look: The unmistakable Penrose rhomb floor: five-fold stars and decagons, never repeating, every tile the same two shapes; with N=4 the octagonal square/rhomb Ammann-Beenker pattern, with N=7 denser quasi-lattices. Edge distance gives grouted tiles; Lookup gives marble per tile. Absolutely nothing on the contact sheet or in the lab is aperiodic and structured.
master.algorithm:
Params: N (4..7, 5 = Penrose P3), Scale, Offsets gamma_k from the seed (generic values, no sum constraint needed: generalised Penrose tilings), Mortar, Output {EdgeDistance, TileType, TileValue, Lookup, VertexDistance}, Source.
Multigrid: unit vectors e_k = (cos 2 pi k/N, sin 2 pi k/N). Multigrid lines: q.e_k + gamma_k = integer. The dual vertex of the multigrid cell with index vector n (n_k = ceil(q.e_k + gamma_k)) is V(n) = sum_k n_k e_k. Each intersection X of lines (j,a) and (k,b) becomes the rhomb with vertices V(n(X)), +e_j, +e_k, +e_j+e_k where n(X) uses the indices of the cell just below X and n_j=a, n_k=b (convention fixed in the proto).
Pointwise location of the rhomb containing P (tiling space): estimate q' = (2/N)(P - sum_k gamma_k e_k) (frame identity sum_k e_k (e_k.q) = (N/2) q). Bound: |V(n(q)) - (N/2) q - sum gamma_k e_k| <= 1.618 for N=5 (max norm of a sum of unit vectors with weights in [0,1)), rhomb diameter < 1.9, so the intersection whose rhomb contains P satisfies |X - q'| < 1.41, i.e. its two line indices are within +-1 of round(q'.e_j + gamma_j) and round(q'.e_k + gamma_k). Candidates: all pairs j<k (10 for N=5) x 9 index offsets = 90. For each: X from a precomputed per-pair 2x2 inverse; n(X) by N ceils (with the j,k entries forced to a,b); V0 = sum n_m e_m (int->float, 2N FMAs); local (alpha,beta) = per-pair precomputed inverse of [e_j e_k] applied to (P - V0); hit = 0<=alpha<1 & 0<=beta<1. Exactly one hit (the dual is a proper tiling for generic gamma). Select outputs by mask.
Outputs: TileType = thick/thin from (k-j) mod N (as -1/+1); TileValue = rnd11(hash(j,k,a,b)); EdgeDistance = parallelogram SDF from (alpha,beta) and the rhomb angle, minus Mortar; Lookup = Source(seed^hash, alpha-0.5, beta-0.5 [, z, w]); VertexDistance = min over the 4 corners (Penrose star/sun motifs).
3D/4D: pattern in (x,y), other axes pass through to the Source.
master.why_new: No combination of existing nodes can produce a tiling with long-range order and no period; even the sum-of-five-cosines quasicrystal interference pattern (a 5-node graph) gives blobs, not tiles. It also makes a hard thing (Penrose textures) a one-node job.
master.simd_plan: Fixed loops: pairs (N(N-1)/2) x 9 candidates x (2x2 solve, N ceils, 2N FMAs, 2x2 solve, compares) all branch-free with mask selects; per-pair constants are small tables computed when N changes. Estimated 3600 flops for N=5: about 20-30 ns per 2D sample on AVX2 (5-7x CellularDistance 2D), 12-18 ns for N=4. Cost does not grow with dimension since z/w pass through.
master.continuity: EdgeDistance and VertexDistance are C0. TileType/TileValue/Lookup are piecewise by design.
master.params: N int, Scale, Seed (drives gamma), Mortar (hybrid), Output enum, Source, LookupScale.
master.risks: The candidate bound (+-1 after rounding, margin 1.41 vs 1.5) and the n(X) convention must be validated by brute force in the proto; non-generic gamma (triple intersections) must be avoided by deriving gamma from the seed with a guard. Cost is high for a building block but fine for a texture; a cheap alternative is Robinson-triangle substitution descent (about 2x Perlin) seeded by a periodic lattice of thick rhombs, which however leaves rare seams of broken tiles along the top-level lattice lines, so I do not recommend it as the primary method.
sources: N.G. de Bruijn, 'Algebraic theory of Penrose's non-periodic tilings of the plane', Indagationes Mathematicae 43 (1981) (cited from memory, not fetched)
master.cost_note: Estimated 3600 flops for N=5: about 20-30 ns per 2D sample on AVX2 (5-7x CellularDistance 2D), 12-18 ns for N=4.

queue.name: QuasiTile
queue.reason: Wild card. True Penrose and Ammann-Beenker tiles via the multigrid dual (J3 top pick). ~3600 flops and 20-30 ns; brute-force validate the candidate bound and compare with the multigrid-noise mosaic.

multigrid-noise.look: Mosaic N=5: flat gray polygons from slivers up to kites, with small rosettes and X-junctions everywhere. Threshold on tile ids gives angular blobs with no streak or hash artifact (std 0.581, uniform would be 0.577). FFT is a 10-arm star from the straight lines. Without a breaker the wide view shows long straight lines running across the whole frame, so the complaint is real. N=3 is periodic kagome, N=4 gives octagonal stars, N=7 and 9 go to fine shards. Parity at N=4 and 5 is bold black and white star ornament. Leaded with phason J=0.9 reads as stained glass: slightly curved lead, local rosettes partly surviving, clean threshold. Polyline wander J=.45 L=2 keeps straight-edged polygons with kinks. LineJitter as specified looks worse: the regular interference goes and the lines stand out. 3D reads as tilted shards in the volume and polygons in the slice. The pillow relief is rows of pointed mounds, not terrain. The idea's Smooth mode was poor: visible straight bands at N=3 and 4 and range -1.43..1.25 with my constant, so I replaced it with a cosine wave sum.
multigrid-noise.dims: Measured: 2D yes. 3D yes (6 icosahedral axes, volume rendered, z-continuity mean .0019 max .0237 leaded). 4D yes as a 5-direction star, run through the torus map (tile4) and a fixed zw slice, edge c0ratio 8.00 on both. Tiling is seamless by construction and no seam shows in the sheet, but seam values were not measured. Polyline wander has a clean form only in 2D; the 3D along-coordinate in the prototype is a fudge.
multigrid-noise.range: -0.999..1.000 over 8 seeds (leaded + phason). Mosaic and Parity -1..1. Edge -1..1 with cap 0.32 clipping.
multigrid-noise.node_shape: MultigridNoise: Families int 3..13 in 2D (3D fixed 6 axes, 4D star table); Output enum {RegionValue, EdgeDistance, Grouted, Parity, LatticeDistance, LatticeManhattan, WaveSum, Lookup}; Grout Width hybrid; Rotation; Line Wander + Wander Length (2D); Phason Amount hybrid + Phason Scale; Source (Lookup only); Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max. Do not ship LineJitter as specified.
multigrid-noise.port_notes: Direct scalar kernels with no Params lookups, harness perlin2 50.2 ns: Mosaic 2.0 ns, polyline leaded 69.8 ns, phason leaded 126.5 ns. The harness speed command is dominated by std::map lookups: Mosaic reads 2.69x perlin there. Edge is exact Euclidean distance with no breaker: max slope measured 6.25 = 2/cap, so unit gradient. With wander, phason or warp it is no longer exact. Seed-derived gamma costs N hashes per lane unless the seed is constant. Eval4 uses normals scaled 1/sqrt2, so its features are 1.41x larger; normalise in a port. N=3 is periodic, say so in the description. Region hash needs N primes: no visible correlation in threshold.

critic.notes: Agree with the prototyper: LineJitter as specified does nothing, confirmed at a second N and seed. Phason or polyline wander or a plain DomainWarp all fix it, so the breaker is convenience, not necessity. The relief (pointed mounds) is not terrain; I tried mode 10 (lookup at dual vertex) as plateau terrain and got polygon plates with a raised grout ridge network, not adopted. Parity N=4 and lattice distance N=4 are reproducible from existing nodes via a 4D cut (see domain-quasicrystal critic), but at 4D source cost; N=5,7 are not reachable by any graph. AVX2 figures remain estimates, no port exists.
critic.improved: Nothing adopted. Added seed-3 wide renders and the N=7 line metric as evidence.

tournament.notes: O(N) line arrangement, 2D/3D/4D, torus map works. Long straight lines without a breaker are real at every seed and N; the idea's line offset does nothing (N=7 seed 3: 86.8 units for none and for J=.25/.45; N=5 seed 42: 90.4 vs 88-90). Polyline wander (8.2u) and a plain Perlin warp (10.8u) both fix it, so a DomainWarp in the graph is an alternative to the breaker. check: mosaic c0 1.0 by design, leaded phason c0 7.91, far and 3D fine. Harness 3.0x perlin plain, 6x phason; direct kernel 2 ns scalar mosaic plausible; AVX2 still estimate. Relief is not terrain. Parity N=4 and lattice distance N=4 are reachable by a 4D Checkerboard/Cellular cut of existing nodes, N=5 and 7 are not. Lattice distance and WaveSum outputs are worth keeping; Lookup at dual vertex is a CellularLookup analogue.
tournament.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE from op counts, not measured. Mosaic or Edge 0.5-1 / 0.7-1.2 / 0.7-1.2 (2D N=5, 3D N=6, 4D N=5). Phason adds 2/3/4 noise evals, about 3 / 8 / 18 total if Perlin. Polyline wander about 3-5, 2D only.

artist-terrain.note: Cheap aperiodic arrangement (sub-ns estimate), but long straight lines without a breaker; analytic lattice distance rosettes are a nice output.

artist-material.note: Busy gray shards and a strange spiky relief, and it needs a warp to hide long lines. Good only as a sci-fi panel base.

voxel-engineer.note: Shard look with long lines needing a warp. Attraction is 0.7-1.2 ns est in 3D, from op counts only. Verify before believing.

maintainer.note: O(N) line arrangement at ~0.5-1 ns est in all dimensions, torus map works. Long straight lines at every seed without the phason breaker, so the breaker is not optional.

graphics-researcher.note: O(N) line arrangement in any dimension with a torus map; needs a breaker for long lines. Analytic lattice-distance rosettes and nested terrazzo are good outputs.

creative.note: Noisy triangle mosaic and a spiky repetitive relief. Far behind quasi-tile by eye.

master.one_liner: N families of parallel 1D lattices (de Bruijn multigrid) instead of a point lattice: aperiodic Penrose-like polygon mosaics, exact edge distance with no window search, and quasi-crystal smooth interference, all in O(N) per sample in any dimension.
master.look:
Mosaic: an aperiodic arrangement of rhombs, pentagons and stars with local 5-/10-fold symmetry (girih / Penrose feel) at N=5; kagome triangles+hexagons at N=3; squares+octagons at N=4; irregular organic polygons with LineJitter. EdgeDistance: crisp crack/mortar networks of straight segments with no cell-size blow-up, inverted = beveled tiles. Smooth: quasi-crystalline rosettes and moire-like interference ridges. Uses: tiled floors, stained glass, basalt/mud cracks that are not Voronoi, alien hull plating, fabric weave (N=2 with jitter), quasi-crystal scientific textures.
[PentagridCells, lattice-kernels] Stained-glass rose windows, 5-fold and 7-fold stars, quasicrystal electron-diffraction feel, pavements, gem facets. Prototyped N=5 and 7: strongly distinct stars and polygons, never exactly repeating, X-junctions everywhere.
master.algorithm:
Params: Families N (default 5), Mode {Mosaic, EdgeDistance, Smooth}, LineJitter J in [0,0.5], Rotation.
Setup (when params change): direction table d_i, i<N. 2D: d_i = (cos(Rotation + i*pi/N), sin(...)). 3D: the 6 icosahedral 5-fold axes normalize(0, +-1, +-phi) perms (N fixed 6) or N Fibonacci-sphere directions. 4D: N directions from a fixed seeded low-discrepancy set on S3. Also per-family offsets gamma_i = rnd01(hash(seed, i)).
Gen(p):
  for i in 0..N-1 (fixed count, unrolled):
    t = dot(p, d_i) + gamma_i
    k = floor(t); f = t - k
    if J > 0: line positions L(k) = k + J*rnd11(hash(seed, i, k)); a = L(k); b = L(k+1); c = L(k-1);
       below = t < a;  lo = Select(below, c, a); hi = Select(below, a, b); k = k - (below?1:0); f = (t-lo)/(hi-lo)
    keep k_i, f_i
  Mosaic:  value = rnd11( hash(seed ^ Sum_i k_i * Prime_i) )            // Prime_i: X,Y,Z,W + 4 more odd constants
  EdgeDistance: e = min_i min(f_i, 1-f_i) * cellWidth_i; value = ScaleOutput(e, 0, 0.5)   // = Euclidean distance to nearest line = distance to region boundary
  Smooth: value = Sum_i hermite1D(k_i, f_i) where hermite1D = quintic lerp of g0*f and g1*(f-1), g0,g1 = rnd11(hash(seed,i,k)), rnd11(hash(seed,i,k+1)); normalize by sqrt(N)*c.
Graph combos (Mosaic * smoothstep(EdgeDistance)) give leaded glass / cracked glaze.

[QuasiCrystalCell, math-physics] Setup: unit normals zeta_j, j=0..N-1 (2D: angle 2 pi j/N for odd N, pi j/N for even N; 3D: 6 icosahedral normals (0,+-1,+-phi)/norm; 4D: 8 normals from the 4D cross-polytope rotated by an irrational matrix). Offsets gamma_j = rnd01(seed,j) - mean (sum 0 gives Penrose, sum 1/2 anti-Penrose).
Gen(seed, x): x' = x/FeatureScale
  for j: t_j = dot(zeta_j, x') + gamma_j ; K_j = Ceil(t_j) ; lam_j = K_j - t_j  (in [0,1))
  Mode RegionValue:  v = hash(seed, K_0..K_{N-1}) -> [-1,1]      (multigrid polygons; quasiperiodic, each region is dual to one tiling vertex)
  Mode GridDistance: v = min_j |lam_j - 0.5| * 2                    (distance to nearest hyperplane of the N-grid: a 5-fold 'star web')
  Mode VertexDistance: z = sum_j K_j zeta_j (dual Penrose vertex, piecewise constant); p' = (N/2) x' + eta, eta = sum_j gamma_j zeta_j ; v = 1 - |p' - z| / rmax   (quasiperiodic bump field with N-fold rosettes)
  Mode PenroseTile (2D only, exact rhomb containing the tiling-space point p=x'):
    y = (p - eta) * (2/N)                       // back-map, since M = sum zeta zeta^T = (N/2) I
    for each pair (r,s) of the N(N-1)/2 families (fixed loop):
      a = dot(zeta_r,y)+gamma_r ; b = dot(zeta_s,y)+gamma_s
      for (kr,ks) in {Floor a, Ceil a} x {Floor b, Ceil b}:            // 4 candidate grid intersections
        xi = solve zeta_r.xi = kr-gamma_r, zeta_s.xi = ks-gamma_s     // 2x2 inverse precomputed per pair
        z0 = sum_j (j==r?kr : j==s?ks : Ceil(dot(zeta_j,xi)+gamma_j)) * zeta_j
        q = p - z0 ; cr = cross(zeta_r,zeta_s)
        u = cross(q,zeta_s)/cr ; v = cross(zeta_r,q)/cr
        inside = (u>=0)&(u<1)&(v>=0)&(v<1)                              // exactly one hit over all candidates
        Select-accumulate: tileType = pair index (thin/thick by |cr|), corner z0, local (u,v)
    Outputs: TileValue = hash(z0 as integer 5-vector) ; TileEdge = min(u,1-u,v,1-v)*|cr| (distance to rhomb edge) ; TileType = thin/thick
3D: RegionValue/GridDistance/VertexDistance with the 6-grid (icosahedral quasicrystal); exact rhombohedra deferred (20 triples x 8 candidates).
master.why_new: Nothing on the sheet is aperiodic-yet-ordered; Cellular always gives convex Voronoi cells and its edge distance (F2-F1) is approximate and window-bound. Here the region boundary distance is exact, costs O(N) with no window, polygons can be non-convex stars, and the cost does not grow as 3^dim: 4D is as cheap as 2D (per-direction dot is the only dim-dependent op).
master.simd_plan: N x (dot, floor, min, int mul, xor). 2D N=5 about 1 ns AVX2 (proto: 1.57x perlin2 scalar with sincos in the loop, which become constants). 3D N=6: about 1.5 ns. 4D N=9: about 3 ns. Direction tables are constants; gamma_j come from seed hash per lane.
master.continuity: Mosaic: discontinuous (piecewise constant). EdgeDistance: C0 (creases on medial lines, like F1). Smooth: C2 (quintic 1D Hermite).
master.params: Families (int 2..8), Mode enum, LineJitter (float), Rotation (float; hybrid optional so the quasi-lattice can twist across space), Feature Scale, Seed Offset, Output Min/Max.
master.risks:
Smooth mode has a star-shaped spectrum (N lines) so it is visibly structured, which is the point but not isotropic. LineJitter with J near 0.5 can make neighbouring lines nearly touch, producing sliver polygons. Mosaic hash tuples with N>4 need extra prime constants; verify no visible correlations.
[PentagridCells, lattice-kernels] Lines are infinite, so a long straight line is visible at wide zoom; combine with a warp when unwanted. N=3 and N=4 degenerate to periodic look unless gamma is irrational-offset. On 4D torus tiling the lines become curves, fine but different look.
[QuasiCrystalCell, math-physics] PenroseTile cost and the 3D exact tiling is heavy; VertexDistance normalisation rmax needs measuring (bounded by (N-2)/2); degenerate gamma giving triple intersections must be avoided by tiny irrational offsets.
sources: N. G. de Bruijn, 'Algebraic theory of Penrose's non-periodic tilings of the plane', 1981 (cited from memory, not fetched)
master.cost_note: 2D N=5 about 1 ns AVX2 (proto: 1.57x perlin2 scalar with sincos in the loop, which become constants).
master.variant_notes: Hash of the N-tuple of line indices. Exact edge distance needs no window. 3D and 4D are cheaper than Perlin, which suits tiling.

queue.name: MultigridNoise
queue.reason: de Bruijn multigrid at ~1 ns with exact edge distance and no window (J4 top pick). Mosaic mode is the keeper; test jitter against the long-straight-lines complaint.

phason-waves.look: N=5 no phason: clean rosettes. N=7 amount 0.4 thresholded: a convincing Turing-like labyrinth of uniform width with a thin FFT ring, and only faint rosette memory in the wide view. At large amount N=5 goes mushy. The 3D icosahedral form with amount 0.3 is a smooth connected cave sponge of fairly even tube width. Relief is regular soft bumps. MultigridNoise mode=8 with breaker=7 is the same formula and gives the same look, so it does not need its own node.

master.one_liner: A latticeless sum of N equal-wavelength plane waves where noise moves perpendicular-space phase: quasi-crystals that rearrange without stretching, down to Turing-like labyrinths.
master.look: Tested. Amount=0, N=5 gives clean five-fold quasi-crystal rosettes. A phonon warp keeps rosettes but bends them. A phason gives a locally ordered pattern whose motifs dissolve and reform while the wavelength stays fixed. N=13 with phason, thresholded, gives a convincing Turing or leopard-maze pattern with uniform feature size, and no lattice to hide. Uses: alien crystals, tiled ornament that never repeats, reaction-diffusion stand-in, narrow-band bases for threshold masks.
master.algorithm:
Table at param-set time: d_j=(cos(j*pi/N),sin(j*pi/N)) and perpendicular star e_j=(cos(j*m*pi/N),sin(j*m*pi/N)), m=2 for N=5 and m coprime with N otherwise. psi_j from hash(seed,j); global rotation from seed.
u=(U(seed,p),U(seed+1,p)).
Out=Sqrt(2/N)*sum_j Cos(k*dot(d_j,p)+k*dot(e_j,u)*Amount+psi_j).
A phonon warp (d_j·u) is plain domain warp and stretches; the phason term (e_j·u) cannot be produced by any warp because it applies a different displacement to each wave.
3D: 6 icosahedral axes for d_j; e_j is the Galois conjugate (swap tau with -1/tau). Threshold bias turns output into spots or labyrinth.
master.why_new: Narrow spectrum (one wavelength everywhere) is something Perlin, Simplex and fractals do not offer, and it is what makes thresholded labyrinths look like Turing patterns. The phason parameter is a domain deformation with no equivalent in the warp family, because features keep their size.
master.simd_plan: No lattice, no hash at Gen time apart from the seed. N Sin+Cos (only Cos needed), N=5..13, plus U source evals (2 / 3 / 3 or 4 for 2D / 3D / 4D). Estimated N=5 about 2-3x Perlin, N=13 about 6x; not measured. Loop count N is constant, so it is allowed. 4D: generic N-direction table such as a 4D 16-cell star.
master.continuity: C-infinity when U is smooth. Not formally checked, but it is a finite sum of Cos of smooth arguments.
master.params: Hybrid: Amount, Frequency, plus phase offset. Int: N, Star Multiplier m. U is an optional source.
master.risks: Direction table and hash per seed: per-lane seeds force recomputation or a global rotation only, so use the node seed or accept the cost. Large phason Amount at N=5 goes mushy, blurring rosettes (visible in the prototype); keep Amount small or use N>=7. Without U the pattern is deterministic and recurs approximately. Sin precision at far coords degrades as with SineWave.
sources: Gardner 1984 and Perlin 1985 sums of sines, Berry 1977 random waves, cut-and-project phason strain from crystallography (all from memory, not consulted)
master.cost_note: Estimated N=5 about 2-3x Perlin, N=13 about 6x; not measured.

The 3D volume is large smooth creased blobs, much less convincing than 2D, and the 3D slice is blurry.

master.one_liner: Average of N triangle-wave pleats at N-fold angles: an aperiodic quasicrystal mirror-facet domain at about the cost of one Perlin.
master.look: Stained-glass polygons and cut-gem facets with straight creases in an aperiodic pattern with 5, 7 or 9-fold local order. With a stripe source it becomes bold polygon contour bands like a topographic map of a crystal. Very different from anything on the contact sheet. Good for crystalline terrain, rock faces, sci-fi plating, masks. Prototyped: mode=1 with N=5, 7.
master.algorithm: q = (2/N) * sum_{i<N} T( dot(p*s, n_i) + o_i ) * n_i, where n_i is at angle pi*i/N, T is a slope +-1 triangle wave with range [-1,1], and o_i is a fixed irrational offset per i. If T(x)=x this is the identity, so T only introduces creases along N line families. Output S(q/s + drift*p). The Jacobian is (2/N) sum +-n_i n_i^T, piecewise constant, so every facet is a linear image of the source, with scale varying per facet. For N not in {1,2,3,4,6} the result is quasi-periodic and has no translational period. Drift (about 0.05-0.1) stops q being confined to a bounded disc.
master.why_new: Hard straight-edged facets with mixed scales and no lattice. Warps only give smooth folds and Cellular only gives convex cells of value. Requires tri-wave fold not expressible in current graph.
master.simd_plan: Loop of constant N: dot, floor, abs, FMulAdd. No hash. About 0.2 ns per direction, so N=5 is about +1 ns in 2D (estimate) plus the source. 3D: 6 icosahedral axes (6D cut-and-project analogue) or 4 cube diagonals. 4D: table of 8-10 directions. Pure function of all inputs, so tileable through the 4D torus with some distortion.
master.continuity: C0 with creases (Lipschitz); measured c0ratio 7.95. C1 option by rounding T near its peaks.
master.params: Directions N (int), Cell Size, Drift (hybrid), Offset Seed (derive o_i from Seed), Source.
master.risks: Zero Jacobian regions stretch source (large blurry facets) at some sign combinations. That is part of the look at low N but can read as out-of-focus patches; fbm sources look less crisp than stripe or ridged sources. Offsets are fixed per seed, so results are a function of seed only through o_i and the source.
master.cost_note: About 0.2 ns per direction, so N=5 is about +1 ns in 2D (estimate) plus the source.

substitution-tiling.look: Pinwheel with mixed depth is the striking one: crystalline shards from huge triangles down to confetti, fans of triangles at vertices, nothing like Voronoi. Uniform Pinwheel D=5 reads as cut gems with a visible direction bias. FFT is a many-armed star, not isotropic. Robinson D=12 gives the same Penrose floor as QuasiTile at a glance, but a detector shows chains of broken half rhombs along the top lattice lines, and it is exactly periodic. Mixed-depth Robinson is a good fractal Penrose shard pattern with 5-fold stars at several scales. Quad is a hashed quadtree that is not aperiodic: flat blocks with strong axis lines. Prism3 slice looks like shards with 2 or 3 dominant line directions and the volume is a hard to read jumble of slabs. The relief is spiked pyramids in deep trenches.
substitution-tiling.dims: Measured: 2D Pinwheel, Robinson and Quad rendered. 3D Prism3, my own dissection: 2M points, 0 outside the child prism, child volume shares .1246-.1252 (expect .125). Oct is written but was not rendered. 4D has no form and the idea's product form was not attempted, so GenTileable2D would not tile.

Decide against the crack family first.
substitution-tiling.port_notes: The headline claim failed at affordable depth. Long leg angle mod pi over 24 bins: D=6 max share .169, D=8 .139, D=10 .122, uniform .042, only 12 bins ever used. Prism3 axis bands at D=8 .218 .005 .344 .062 .372, uniform .2 each. Straight runs: Pinwheel D=5 30.8 units, D=7 25.3 units, 17-18% of edge pixels on runs over 8 units. Robinson stop=0 is periodic: translation by top lattice vectors kept tile type and edge distance at 100.00% of samples at D=8 and D=12; seed gives 100.00% identical geometry, so seed is only an offset. Broken half rhomb area: D=6 5.52%, D=8 1.82%, D=10 .75%, D=12 .26%, D=14 .12%. Thick:thin area 2.6264. Direct scalar: Pinwheel D=5 96.3, D=7 116.6; Robinson D=8 117.3, D=12 151.6, D=16 161.0; Prism3 D=4 119.7, perlin3 104.5, worley3 148.4. These are branchy, so the mispredicts inflate them. Prism3 rotation group claim is from my memory of Conway and Radin and is not checked against the paper. Mixed-depth grout needs the Robinson diagonal counted as an edge.

critic.notes: Pinwheel's selling point (infinitely many orientations) is not reached at affordable depth, and the result shows two dominant directions and long straight lines. Robinson stop=0 is periodic with visible broken half rhomb chains, so it is not the Penrose route; QuasiTile is. The mixed-depth shard looks are striking and not available elsewhere, which is why this is showcase rather than drop, but a BSP shatter from the crack family covers the same artistic ground with fewer defects. Not worth a node.

master.one_liner: Pointwise descent through a substitution tiling (pinwheel 1:2 right triangles with irrational rotations, or quad/octree), with hashed per-tile stop depth, outputting tile value, edge distance, orientation, or a Source stamped into each tile's local frame.
master.look:
A crisp tiling of congruent triangles at mixed sizes (adaptive stop), where tile orientation is irrationally distributed so no two regions line up, yet every edge is shared exactly (T-junctions, no cracks, unlike Voronoi subdivision). Stamp mode gives a 'quilt' of a pattern repeated in randomly rotated, exactly congruent patches at several scales (parquet, shattered glass, aperiodic mosaics, roof tiles, circuit die). Quad mode gives a clean hashed quadtree (Mondrian, pixel-sorting, city blocks) with 3D octree support. Nothing on the sheet has exact congruent tiles with dense rotations.
[PinwheelCells, lattice-kernels] Radiating fans of triangles, stained glass, crystalline facets; hillshade reads as cut gems. Prototyped at depth 4, 5, 7: at depth 7 base rectangle is invisible and no axis direction stands out. Important detail found during prototyping: the naive midpoint split yields all five children mirrored, so orientations cancel on even depth and look axis aligned. The H-M3 diagonal split is required.
master.algorithm:
Canonical tile T: right angle at O(0,0), long leg to X(2,0), short leg to Y(0,1). Top level: lattice of 2x1 rectangles of size S; cell (ix,iy) with local (u,v)=(frac*2, frac): lower-left triangle if u/2+v<1 -> (x,y)=(u,v) else (x,y)=(2-u,1-v); h = HashPrimes(ix,iy) ^ diagonal bit. Then for d in 1..MaxDepth (uniform loop):
  // pinwheel split: altitude foot H=(0.4,0.8); 1 small tile OHY + big triangle OHX split into 4 medial tiles
  small = (y > 2x)
  tile0: x0 = 2 - x - 2y ;  y0 = y - 2x                     // scale sqrt5, reflected
  big  : xb = x - 0.5y ;    yb = 1 - 0.5x - y                // scale sqrt5/2
  B = xb > 1 ; C = yb > 0.5 ; A = (xb + 2yb < 1) ; D = otherwise
  (xA,yA)=(2xb,2yb) (xB,yB)=(2xb-2,2yb) (xC,yC)=(2xb,2yb-1) (xD,yD)=(2-2xb,1-2yb)
  idx = Select chain 0..4 ; (x,y) = Select chain ; hNew = Hash(h, idx)
  stop = (d >= MinDepth) & (rnd01(hNew) < StopProb)  ; frozen |= stop (per-lane mask)
  (x,y,h,scale) = Select(frozen, old, new); scale *= sqrt5 where !frozen
  (also push a unit vector e=(1,0) through the same linear maps for the orientation output)
Outputs (enum): TileValue = rnd11(h);  EdgeDistance = S/scale * min(y, x, (2 - x - 2y)/sqrt5);  Orientation = e.x (cosine of tile angle, dense in [-1,1] for pinwheel);  Stamp = Source(x*StampScale + hashOffset, y*StampScale) i.e. the Source rendered in each tile's own congruent frame; Mortar = smoothstep(EdgeDistance/Width) * TileValue.
Quad/Oct mode: same loop with 4/8 children (x,y[,z]) = 2*frac - floor, trivially 3D. Pinwheel 3D: evaluate in xy with the z slab index folded into the top-level hash (extrusion); honest fallback, not isotropic.
master.why_new:
Only known family of tilings with congruent tiles and uniformly distributed orientations. Isotropy comes from geometry, not jitter. Fans of up to many triangles around a vertex are not reachable by Voronoi, BSP or warps. Cost is independent of any window.
[SubstitutionTiling, hierarchy-multiscale] Voronoi-based patch nodes (CellularLookup, shatter/BSP variants) have irregular cells and cracks or hard borders; this gives exact hierarchical subdivision with irrational orientations, pointwise, with a user Source stamped in tile frames. Quadtree/octree with hashed stop is the 'adaptive subdivision by hash' primitive in its simplest exact form.
master.simd_plan: Depth loop with constant count, 5-way child select via masks then 6 table values per lane (Select chain or permute table). Scalar at depth 4: 1.9x perlin2, 0.9x worley2 with branches. Port estimate 2-3 ns 2D at depth 5. 3D: Conway-Radin quaquaversal prism dissection (8 children, ratio 1/2) with dense rotation group, needs a table derived and verified. 4D: product form min(d(x,y), d(z,w)) with hashed combined id, enough for GenTileable2D seamlessness.
master.params: Tiling enum {Pinwheel, Quad}, MaxDepth int, MinDepth int, StopProb hybrid (0 = uniform depth), Output enum, Edge Width, Stamp Scale, Source (optional), Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
master.risks:
Pinwheel top level is a visibly axis-aligned rectangle lattice until depth>=3; apply a fixed irrational rotation of the top lattice. Reflections are part of the pinwheel; Stamp of a chiral pattern will show mirrored copies (could be a toggle). Cumulative float error at depth>8 at far coordinates; clamp depth to 8.
[PinwheelCells, lattice-kernels] Without the stochastic variant geometry repeats every sqrt5^Depth*2 units and does not change with seed; base seams become visible at low depth. Depth above about 8 loses float precision in far coords (remap multiplies by sqrt5 each level). 3D dissection not yet verified. The 3D form may be weaker than 2D.
master.cost_note: Scalar at depth 4: 1.9x perlin2, 0.9x worley2 with branches. Port estimate 2-3 ns 2D at depth 5.
master.variant_notes: Pinwheel needs the H-M3 split: the naive midpoint split makes all five children mirrored and looks axis aligned (found in the PinwheelCells prototype).

master.one_liner: Cut-and-project: 2D position becomes a 4D source sample along 4 symmetric directions, so any lattice-based 4D source (Value, Perlin, Cellular, Checkerboard, SineWave) shows 8-, 10- or 12-fold aperiodic quasicrystal order.
master.look: Penrose / Ammann-Beenker / dodecagonal aperiodic patterns: local 8/10/12-fold rosettes that never repeat, Islamic girih vibes with Checkerboard or Value sources, aperiodic Voronoi-like cells with Cellular, interference quasicrystals with SineWave. Nothing on the sheet has rotational order above 4-fold, and nothing is aperiodic with long-range order.
master.algorithm:
Params: Symmetry enum {Octagonal(8), Decagonal(10/5), Dodecagonal(12)}, Scale, Phase (4 floats, hybrid ok), Rotation.
Precompute 4 unit directions e_j (2D): Octagonal: angles j*pi/4, j=0..3; Decagonal: 2*pi*j/5, j=1..4 (Euler totient phi(5)=phi(8)=phi(12)=4, so Z^4 suffices for all three); Dodecagonal: j*pi/6, j=0..3.

  (x,y) rotated by Rotation, scaled: q = p / Scale
  X_j = Dot(q, e_j) + Phase_j         for j = 0..3          // 8 FMAs
  return Source.Gen(seed, X_0, X_1, X_2, X_3)               // 4D source

Why it works: the image plane is a totally irrational 2-plane of Z^4 that is invariant under the k-fold rotation acting as a signed coordinate permutation (e.g. octagonal: rotating by 45 deg maps (a,b,c,d) -> (-d,a,b,c)). The cell walls x_j = integer of any cubic-lattice source project to 4 families of parallel lines at the symmetric angles, i.e. de Bruijn's multigrid, whose dual is the Ammann-Beenker (8), Penrose (5/10) or Socolar (12) tiling. Cellular/Value in 4D therefore produce aperiodic rhombus-like cells; SineWave 4D gives the textbook quasicrystal interference pattern.
3D input: X_j = Dot(q.xy, e_j) + z * e_perp_j (z slides the cut through the lattice => phason flips: the pattern locally rearranges continuously), so animating z morphs between valid quasicrystals; 4D: w adds a second phason axis. (True icosahedral 3D needs 6D: not available.)
master.why_new: Lattice sources are inherently 4-fold (square) or 6-fold (simplex) periodic; this one-node change turns them into quasi-periodic structures with forbidden symmetries, at the cost of one 4D evaluation and 8 FMAs. Not expressible by any combination of existing nodes (AddDimension cannot make the irrational 2-plane).
master.simd_plan: 8 FMAs + a 4D source eval; cost dominated by the source (Perlin 4D 4.3 ns, Value 4D cheaper, Cellular 4D 41 ns). No lattice window of its own. Uses the existing 4D Gen path of every source, so it also pressures 4D performance work.
master.continuity: As the source (the map is linear).
master.params: Symmetry enum, Scale float, Phase 4 floats (hybrid: a noise-driven phase gives slow phason wobble), Rotation float.
master.risks: Generic smooth sources (Perlin/Simplex) look only subtly quasi-symmetric; the effect shines with lattice-aligned sources, so ship presets. Cellular 4D is expensive. Features along different e_j directions have equal scale only if the source is isotropic across its 4 axes.
master.cost_note: 8 FMAs + a 4D source eval; cost dominated by the source (Perlin 4D 4.3 ns, Value 4D cheaper, Cellular 4D 41 ns).

proto_index.params_text: AddDimension(Source=AddDimension(Source=Checkerboard(Feature Scale=24), New Dimension Position=Gradient(Multiplier X=0.7071, Multiplier Y=0.7071)), New Dimension Position=Gradient(Multiplier X=-0.7071, Multiplier Y=0.7071))

queue.name: DomainQuasicrystal
queue.reason: Cut-and-project to a 4D source in 8 FMAs turns any lattice source quasi-periodic. Strong on Value and Cellular, subtle on smooth sources; Cellular 4D costs ~41 ns.
